## Proposed implementation and validation — subject to this review

The initial proposal uses the existing CounterRepository API and a fixed maximum of 1000 entries. It adds a private Map per repository object; access refreshes recency and insertion above the cap evicts the least recently used key. Use Map.has() to distinguish a cached absent counter from a cache miss. This is proposed work, not implemented or approved.

Retain invalidation on write. A successful set invalidates cached reads; the next get obtains SQLite's stored scalar before caching it. Do not replace invalidation with write-through of the caller's value, which can change SQLite round-trip behavior such as signed zero.

One process does not imply one CounterRepository or one Database object. Proposed conservative coherence: a module-wide write token changes only after any repository set commits. Each instance compares its last-seen token before serving cached values and clears its map if it changed. This supports other repository objects and handles in the same process without assuming one constructor call. It also clears unrelated instance caches; assess that deliberate simplicity/performance tradeoff. External writes remain outside the existing module contract.

Before implementation is accepted, compare the cached implementation against the current repository on the same deterministic traces: cold/hot and absent reads; set-after-hit and set-after-absence; two repositories observing each other's committed writes; two handles to one temporary SQLite file; eviction and recency above 1000 entries; invalid input, numeric round trips and database errors. Preserve the existing example and error/return contracts. Do not claim these tests already exist or pass; any mismatch is a review finding to resolve.

Add a reproducible benchmark and query-count harness comparing the current repository with the proposal, using repeated-hot-key, absent-key, mixed-write and mostly-unique-key traces at the same capacity. Record SELECT counts, elapsed time and cache memory rather than assuming embedded SQLite is a bottleneck. A repeated trace should reduce actual SELECT executions without changing results; quantify the invalidation and scan costs. State the benefit/acceptance evidence in the reviewed plan instead of inventing measured improvements.
